name: Black Forest gateau
origin: Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte, named for the Black Forest region of southwestern Germany, known for its cherries and kirsch (cherry brandy); layers of chocolate sponge with whipped cream, cherries and kirsch.

ingredients.note: cocoa fraction of a 15%-of-flour cocoa dose, split as in devils-food.json

process.name: whip eggs and sugar
process.description: whip whole eggs with sugar over a bain-marie to full ribbon-stage volume

process.name: fold in flour and cocoa
process.description: sift flour and cocoa together and fold into the whipped egg foam

process.name: fold in butter
process.description: fold in cooled melted butter last

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in round pans, then split into thin layers once cooled

notes: The genoise-method sponge here is chocolate-adjusted (cocoa split by fat/solids as in devils-food.json) but otherwise the same foam-cake proportion as genoise.json — this is the real relationship: a Black Forest gateau's sponge layers are a cocoa genoise. The whipped-cream filling, cherries and kirsch that define the finished cake are separately-prepared components layered on after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
